result.topic_en: Pages 112–113 work an example: finding the relation between x and y that makes the integral of dx√(1+pp)/√y a maximum or minimum, which yields a cycloid. The text then re-examines the analysis by distinguishing the ordinary differential d (moving along the curve) from the variation δ (passing from the principal to the varied state), with δx = 0.
result.transcription:
112 DE METHODO
XXIX.
Quia exemplo haec clariora euadent, quaeratur relatio inter $x$ et $y$, vt posito $x=a$ haec formula $\int\frac{dx\surd(1+pp)}{\surd y}$, existente $p=\frac{dy}{dx}$, maximum minimumve obtineat valorem. Cum ergo sit $Z=\frac{\surd(1+pp)}{\surd y}$, erit $M=0$, $N=-\frac{\surd(1+pp)}{2y\surd y}$ et $P=\frac{p}{\surd y\surd(1+pp)}$, sicque primo adimplenda est haec aequatio $N-\frac{dP}{dx}=0$, seu $Ndx-dP=0$, quae per $p$ multiplicata dat $Ndy=pdP$. At ob $M=0$ est $dZ=Ndy+Pdp$, ideoque $dZ=pdP+Pdp$, quae integrata praebet $Z=Pp+C$, seu $\frac{\surd(1+pp)}{\surd y}=\frac{pp}{\surd y\surd(1+pp)}+C$ hoc est $\frac{1}{\surd y\surd(1+pp)}=C=\frac{1}{\surd b}$. Hinc porro nanciscimur $b=y(1+pp)$ et $p=\surd\frac{b-y}{y}=\frac{dy}{dx}$, ita vt sit $dx=\frac{ydy}{\surd(by-yy)}$ et integrando $x=c-\surd(by-yy)+bA\,\sin.\frac{2\surd(by-yy)}{b}$. Verum ad pleniorem determinationem debet esse $P=0$, posito $x=a$, hoc est $p=0$, et $y=b$; vnde positis $x=a$, et $y=b$, constans $c$ ita definitur, vt fit $c=a-\pi b$. Ac si velimus, vt posito $x=0$ fiat et $y=0$, debet esse $b=\frac{a}{\pi}$.
XXX.
Antequam hanc inuestigationem analyticam ad casus, quibus functio $Z$ etiam formulas integrales in se complectitur, accommodemus, ipsam analysin, qua hactenus sumus vsi, diligentius examinemus, ac momenta, quibus innititur, accuratius perpendamus. Versatur autem haec Analysis circa duas variabiles $x$ et $y$, quae partim ad statum, quem vocaui principalem, partim ad statum variatum referuntur, ita vt earum altera $x$ ad vtrumque statum aeque pertineat, altera vero

MAXIMORVM ET MINIMORVM. 113
vero $y$, dum a statu principali ad variatum transfertur, incrementum capiat $\delta y$, dum autem in eodem statu ad valorem $x+dx$ promouetur, augmentum differentiale consuetum $dy$ accipiat; hinc si variabilis $y$ simul a statu principali in variatum et locum ipsi $x+dx$ respondentem promoueatur, augmentum eius erit $dy+\delta y$. Cum autem $x$ ad vtrumque statum aeque referatur, erit $\delta x=0$.
XXXI.
Si iam habeatur alia quaecunque functio $V$ ad locum $x$ in statu principali relata, eaque in eodem statu ad locum $x+dx$ promoueatur, eius incrementum, quod ei accedet, more solito per $dV$ exprimamus. Sin autem ea, manente valore ipsius $x$ eodem, e statu principali in variatum proferatur, eius augmentum nouo more per $\delta V$ exponamus. Quodsi iam functio illa $V$ sit ex quantitatibus $x, y, p, q, r$ etc. vtcunque composita, litterae autem $p, q, r$ etc. eiusmodi quantitates designent, quarum vtraque incrementa $dp$, $dq$, $dr$ etc. et $\delta p$, $\delta q$, $\delta r$ etc. exhiberi queant; hinc consueto differentiandi modo etiam ambo incrementa functionis $V$ assignari poterunt. Si enim fuerit, pro translatione a loco $x$ ad locum $x+dx$, in eodem statu, ex differentiatione consueta
$dV=Mdx+Ndy+Pdp+Qdq+Rdr+$ etc.
erit, pro translatione a statu principali in variatum, eodem vero loco $x$, existente, vti notauimus, $\delta x=0$,
$\delta V=M\delta x+N\delta y+P\delta p+Q\delta q+R\delta r$ etc.
Tom. X. Nou. Comm. P XXXII.

items.english: Let the relation between x and y be sought such that, when x = a, the formula ∫dx√(1+pp)/√y, where p = dy/dx, attains a maximum or minimum value.

items.quote: Antequam hanc inuestigationem analyticam ad casus, quibus functio $Z$ etiam formulas integrales in se complectitur, accommodemus, ipsam analysin, qua hactenus sumus vsi, diligentius examinemus
items.english: Before we adapt this analytic investigation to cases in which the function Z itself contains integral formulas, let us examine more carefully the analysis we have used so far.

items.quote:
Si enim fuerit, pro translatione a loco $x$ ad locum $x+dx$, in eodem statu, ex differentiatione consueta
$dV=Mdx+Ndy+Pdp+Qdq+Rdr+$ etc.
erit, pro translatione a statu principali in variatum, eodem vero loco $x$, existente, vti notauimus, $\delta x=0$,

items.english: For if, for the passage from position x to position x+dx in the same state, ordinary differentiation gives dV = Mdx + Ndy + Pdp + Qdq + Rdr + etc., then for the passage from the principal state to the varied state at the same position x (where, as we noted, δx = 0), we will have δV = Mδx + Nδy + Pδp + Qδq + Rδr etc.
